content:
marta: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector heuristic landed, prod p99 for short seq (~64 tokens) climbed from ~220ms -> ~340ms on r4-gpu pool.
lee: saw spikes too, users flagged higher tail. Is this microbatch sizing or kernel fallback?
sasha: first guess: selector now prefers large-block matmul for medium seq, but continuous-batching holds requests longer to hit token cap -> worse tail for short requests.
jamie: can we confirm scheduler params? current on r4: max_batch_tokens=4096, max_wait_ms=6 as default.
marta: i fetched overrides — r4-pool had max_batch_tokens=8192 and max_wait_ms=12 (why?). that explains extra queue time.
perf-bot: perf-alert: p99_latency spike detected 2026-03-16T22:18Z — +54% vs baseline — dashboard: https://dashboards/perf/incident/abc123
lee: increasing max_wait_ms will force continuous batching to wait to fill batches by tokens not count -> short requests suffer.
sasha: also consider KV cache behavior: new-convo seed misses can push selector into slower kernel path (more memcpy / different tiling).
jamie: quick experiment plan: reduce max_wait_ms to 3 on one canary rack and cap max_batch_tokens to 2048. also tweak kernel_selector threshold for 'block_dense' to trigger only for seq>128.
marta: i'll prod a reproducer: synthetic load with 80% single-turn 32-token prompts, 20% long tails. will capture microbatch histograms + kernel_choice logs.
lee: add tracing headers and kv metrics: enable `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kv,kernel,queue` for the canary so we can correlate kv_hit -> kernel -> latency.
sasha: also run perf flamegraphs on the KV miss path; int8 kernels sometimes incur extra conversion memcpy.
jamie: schedule: canary @ 23:00 UTC. steps: 1) patch scheduler config 2) enable tracing 3) run 300 qps synthetic 4) collect p50/p95/p99 + microbatch size distribution.
marta: pushed PR with scheduler change (yaml):
```yaml
sched:
  pools:
    r4-pool:
      max_wait_ms: 3
      max_batch_tokens: 2048
```
PR: https://github.com/redwood/scheduler/pull/1234
deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued for r4-pool at 23:01 UTC by marta. :rocket:
perf-bot: suggestion: also try lowering microbatch_target_tokens from 256 -> 128 for this pool to bias smaller microbatches.
lee: if p99 improves but throughput drops, we can add burst capacity policy for peak windows.
sasha: note: smaller batches might slightly lower KV hit_rate initially; watch token-cost impact.
jamie: we'll A/B for 1 hour and revert if throughput loss >10% or p99 doesn't drop >=20%.
marta: i'll paste logs once canary finishes.
--- canary results ---
marta: canary finished. quick numbers: p99 dropped from ~340ms -> ~240ms; p50 ~unchanged. throughput -6% under synthetic. microbatch avg requests/batch: 5 -> 3.
lee: KV hit_rate dipped 0.92 -> 0.88 first 5m then warmed to ~0.91 after 10m.
sasha: kernel_choice distribution: fewer block_dense picks, more small GEMM path. flamegraphs show reduced memcpy on hot path.
jamie: takeaway: lowering max_wait_ms helped tail at modest throughput cost. propose adaptive policy: lower max_wait_ms when short-seq ratio > 60% and p95 trending up.
marta: filing follow-up RFC and adding console metrics (per-pool p95 vs avg batch size) so teams can choose 'latency-tilted' vs 'throughput-tilted' presets.
perf-bot: RFC link: https://go/redwood/rfc/scheduler-adaptive-maxwait
lee: follow-ups: (1) try microbatch_target_tokens=128 A/B, (2) add kernel_selector telemetry to console, (3) evaluate automated per-pool max_wait_ms tuning based on recent p95.
sasha: +1. i'll own kernel telemetry dashboard. @jamie can you add the microbatch histograms to the perf pipeline?
jamie: yup, will add histo export and a small script to compute avg/median/mode microbatch size per minute.
marta: thanks everyone. keeping this thread as the timeline; filing the postmortem/notes shortly. :white_check_mark:
